correctness.rationale: For every fixed d>=3, normalize the full-dimensional parent by an affine map. Equality of daughter and parent volumes requires a permutation barycentric matrix; compactness isolates disjoint near-permutation neighborhoods. Writing off-diagonal coordinates t>=0 and S=sum t, the exact second-order determinant term is 1-det(A)=S-B2(t)+O_d(S^3), where B2=sum_{i<j}(s_i s_j-t_ij t_ji). Along t=Sp, radial inversion gives S_epsilon(p)=epsilon+epsilon^2 B2(p)+O_d(epsilon^3) uniformly. Uniform Dirichlet mixed moments E[p_a p_b]=1/[m(m+1)] imply the relative coefficient m(d^2-1)/[2(m+1)], and disjoint (d+1)! orientations give the leading constant (d+1)!(d!)^(d+1)/m!. Dominated convergence of epsilon^-1 t gives uniform law on the m-simplex and deficit Beta(m,1). Independently recomputed exact constants: d=3 1/15400 with correction 48/13; d=4 1/2546168625 with correction 50/7. These finite checks are supplementary to the uniform fixed-d analytic argument.

originality.rationale: The asserted new content is the two-term near-maximal volume tail in every fixed dimension d>=3 and the conditional joint barycentric shape law. It is not the full volume law, moment calculation, nested-simplex limit, or high-dimension sample-count theorem. Alagar already covers the planar triangle distribution, and that dimension is expressly excluded. Mannion studies the same random daughter tetrahedron in d=3 and is the serious priority comparator; only its abstract and bibliographic material were available, so potential full-paper overlap is not excluded. Published-research semantic search found related but non-covering simplex spectra and sections. Best-of-knowledge originality PASS with a major named risk, rather than treating access alone as mathematical rejection.
